message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to call out my coworker Jackson for lying about his boxing and martial arts skills. Let me start by understanding the situation better. Jackson works with me, and he's always bragging about how he was a top-notch boxer with a 23-0 record, one of the best in the valley. He also talks about how he could kick anyone's ass and how he used to be in great shape before he got out of his prime and became flabby. I know for a fact that most of this is probably not true because if he was really that good, there should be some records or mentions online when I Google his name. But when I do, nothing comes up. I'm 19 years old and have been training in Muay Thai for eight years, and I also wrestled in high school. I'm very fit and proud of my progress in martial arts and fitness. I used to be overweight too, so I understand the struggle, but I've worked hard to get where I am now. I rarely hang out with Jackson outside of work because he never stops talking about his supposed achievements and other lies, like getting kicked out of culinary school for fighting or knowing high-profile gang bangers who make millions, which is why he works in this restaurant just for fun and not because he needs the money. Last weekend, we were hanging out, having a few beers, and watching UFC. During the Blagoy Ivanov vs. Taimur Iasaf fight, Jackson said, "I could KO both these bums, no challenge." That's when I snapped and told him I doubted he could even kick my ass, especially since I'm 19 and half his weight. I also called him out on his boxing bullshit and mentioned that nothing shows up when I Google his name. I challenged him to come down to my Muay Thai gym and try, saying I would "maul" him. He got all pissy and walked out, and then I told some of my coworkers about it. Most of them think I'm a asshole, although a few agreed with me. So, the question is: Is it right or wrong for me to call him out like that? And why? First, I need to consider the context. We were hanging out, having beers, so it was a casual setting. But Jackson is an adult, 29 years old, and I'm 19. There's a significant age difference, and he's my coworker. Calling him out in front of others, especially in a public setting like watching UFC, could have been seen as confrontational or disrespectful. On the other hand, I was frustrated with his constant lying and bragging, especially about areas where I have genuine expertise and pride in my achievements. It's understandable that I wanted to stand up for myself and not let his lies go unchallenged. But by calling him out publicly, I risked damaging our working relationship, and it's possible that others saw my actions as immature or unnecessarily confrontational. Even though some coworkers agreed with me, the majority thought I was a asshole, which suggests that my approach might have been perceived as inappropriate. I also need to think about the potential consequences. If Jackson feels disrespected, he might take it out on me at work, or our relationship could become tense. Additionally, by sharing the incident with coworkers, I might have contributed to a negative workplace environment. Perhaps a better approach would have been to address the issue privately, without the public confrontation. That way, I could express my feelings without risking workplace harmony or appearing confrontational. In summary, while it's understandable to want to stand up against someone who's lying and bragging, especially in areas where you have personal expertise, the manner in which you do so is crucial. Publicly calling someone out, especially in a workplace setting, can be seen as disrespectful and can lead to negative consequences. It might have been more effective to handle the situation privately or to find a way to address the issue without confrontation. So, considering all this, I think it was somewhat wrong to call him out in that manner because it could have been handled more respectfully and privately, avoiding potential workplace conflict and maintaining a better relationship with my coworker.
